name: Genetic Primary Orthostatic Hypotension

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic Criteria for Genetic Primary Orthostatic Hypotension

criteria.description: Sustained drop in systolic blood pressure ≥20 mmHg or diastolic ≥10 mmHg within 3 minutes of standing
Exclusion of secondary causes of orthostatic hypotension such as medication effects or systemic disease
Positive family history consistent with autosomal dominant or recessive inheritance
Abnormal autonomic function tests demonstrating impaired sympathetic vasoconstriction

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of sustained orthostatic blood pressure drop and exclusion of secondary causes, supported by abnormal autonomic testing; family history supportive but not mandatory
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing may confirm diagnosis but is not required for clinical diagnosis

pathognomonic.symptomName: Orthostatic hypotension with symptomatic cerebral hypoperfusion
searchTerms: low blood pressure on standing causing symptoms
faintness due to low standing BP
poor heart rate and blood pressure control
tiredness from low brain blood flow
fatigue due to poor cerebral perfusion
head pain related to orthostatic shifts

occasional.symptomName: Cold extremities due to autonomic dysfunction
searchTerms: cold hands and feet from nerve dysfunction
chilly extremities due to autonomic failure
cold limbs caused by nerve problems

rare.symptomName: Gastrointestinal dysmotility symptoms (e.g., early satiety, nausea)
Mild cognitive impairment secondary to chronic hypoperfusion
searchTerms: slight cognitive decline from low brain blood flow
thinking difficulties due to chronic hypoperfusion
too little or too much sweating

laboratory: Normal routine blood tests excluding secondary causes
Possible abnormal catecholamine levels on standing
imaging: Brain MRI usually normal; used to exclude other causes
genetic: Mutations in genes affecting autonomic nervous system function (e.g., DBH gene mutations)
other: Autonomic function testing showing impaired sympathetic vasoconstriction
Tilt-table test demonstrating orthostatic hypotension without heart rate compensatory increase

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of underlying systemic disease or medication cause
Improvement upon treatment of secondary cause
Progressive autonomic failure with additional symptoms such as urinary dysfunction
Usually adult onset with no family history

redFlags: Presence of neurological deficits suggestive of central nervous system pathology
Failure to respond to standard supportive measures
